reports.title: SOMNIGROUP INTERNATIONAL INC. REPORTS RECORD THIRD QUARTER 2026 RESULTS

guidance.heading: Financial Guidance
section: For the full year 2026, the Company revised its expectations for adjusted EPS to a range of $2.85 to $2.95, which represents an approximate 7% increase from 2025 adjusted EPS at the mid-point of the range.

desk.headline: Sales up 11% to $2.35bn on Leggett deal but below estimates; adj. EPS $1.04 just short; 2026 EPS outlook cut to $2.85–2.95
results: Growth came from the Leggett & Platt purchase (closed 26 Aug), which added $372.6m of sales; the existing businesses shrank — Mattress Firm and Tempur Sealy North America each -5.8%, International -12.3%.
UK chain Dreams saw sales drop 34.7% after a troubled new ERP system went live; International operating margin fell to 9.4% from 18.1%.
Adjusted gross margin slipped to 43.0% from 45.6% on lower-margin Leggett sales, while North America's jumped to 65.5% helped by tariff refunds and synergies.
GAAP EPS fell 10.8% to $0.74 on $35.5m of deal costs and a $13.0m debt refinancing loss; adjusted EPS rose 9.5% to a record $1.04.
Leverage improved to 2.69x; quarterly dividend held at $0.17 a share.

guidance.summary: Full-year 2026 adjusted EPS is now expected at $2.85–2.95, down from $2.85–3.15 given in August — the top of the range was cut. On the call management also pointed to about $8.65bn of net sales and about $1.4bn of adjusted EBITDA for the year.

points: Management tied the cut to Dreams (about $25m less EBITDA in the second half), roughly $15m of extra transport costs and a bedding market it expects to shrink by mid-single digits.
Dreams' system problems should be fixed by early Q1 2027; about $20m of tariff refunds arrived early and offset the Dreams hit.
Demand improved through the quarter and early Q4 trends at Mattress Firm were slightly better, though entry-level shoppers remain under financial strain.
Leggett is targeted to add about $125m of adjusted EBITDA from 2027; Mattress Firm plans to grow to over 2,500 stores starting in 2027.
Management sketched a path to about $3.40 of EPS run-rate exiting 2027 and may raise prices in early 2027 if petroleum-linked costs stay high.
